name: Ultra orange, 747s (1979)
description: The 747s' version of Braniff International's 1978 'Ultra' scheme, worn by every Braniff 747 but N601BN in 1979 (the 747-200s, the leased 747-100 N610BN and the 747SPs): the whole aircraft a deep orange, belly included (no silver belly or belly pinstripes), the fin, rudder and tailplane orange, with a broad cream-gold pinstripe and a thin dark red one just inside the fin's leading edge. 'BRANIFF INTERNATIONAL' in large cream-gold upright capitals (wide, geometric, of even stroke) over the forward main-deck windows, from about 10.4 m back to well behind the second door, just under the upper deck's windows. Orange nacelles with cream and red bands behind polished lips. Gray wings.

sources.title: Yesterday's Airlines: The Elegance Campaign, Braniff's Ultra Look
sources.note: Evidence only: Ultra unveiled 17 July 1978; eight darker colors (terra cotta, Perseus green, Mercury blue, metallic blue, light Corvette blue, chocolate brown, burgundy, sparkling burgundy); the 25 727s delivered from April 1978 in Ultra, only 12 older 727s repainted; all but two DC-8-62s repainted; the 747s in an orange version with a solid orange belly, except N601BN; a mix of Ultra and Flying Colors to the end in 1982.

sources.title: Yesterday's Airlines: Flying Colors, Braniff's 727-227 Advanceds
sources.note: Evidence only: Flying Colors from late 1971, two tones in four pairs (red/Aztec gold, orange/ochre, green/light green, blue/light blue), seen almost only on 727s.

sources.title: The Airliner Modeling Site forum: 'Ultra-era' memories (Braniff)
sources.note: Evidence only: colors per airframe from members' memories and slides (N426BN metallic blue and N404BN sparkling burgundy from about 1978; DC-8s N1809E chocolate, N1807 burgundy, N802BN Mercury blue, N801BN and N1806 Corvette blue, N1805 terra cotta, N1803 and N1804 Perseus green; N412BN terra cotta in 1979) and the planned pinstripe pairs.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Braniff International Airways
sources.note: Evidence only: the fleet (115 aircraft in December 1979; 747-200Bs from 1978, 747SPs from 1979, ten DC-8-62s, 79 727-200s over the years), the Ultra colors with Halston and Harper and George, 'INTERNATIONAL' dropped from the 727s' and DC-8s' Ultra titles but kept on the 747s, Calder's painted aircraft.

titles.style: Braniff's 1970s 'International' capitals in cream-gold: upright, wide and geometric (round O and C, pointed A's and V-less N's), of even, middling weight, with a double space between the words; over the forward main-deck windows.

notes: Measured 2026-11-24 for ghost flights on 747-230B N611BN (June 1979, right side, high resolution; fitted to shapes/B744-passenger.json by the nose, doors 1 and 5 and the fin's tip, within 2 px). Drawn on the 747-100/-200 shape (shapes/B742.json: the 747-400's main deck, the short upper deck, no winglets); the 747SPs (N603BN-N606BN) are much shorter. The title re-measured 2026-11-25 on the same photo by doors 1 to 3 and against the main deck's and the upper deck's window rows: 10.35 to 27.8 m back, capitals 0.92 m tall (23-26 px, growing toward the nose), the baseline 1.38 m above the centerline, its tops just under the upper deck's three windows (it had been drawn 1.9 m tall, up across them). The fin's pinstripe runs on along the fin's top and the tailplane's leading edge on the photo; only the leading edge's run is drawn. The nacelles' bands are read off a small part of the photo and are approximate. N611BN's slide is red-shifted (it reads red); the orange is N602BN's (1980) and the 747SPs', the 'Big Orange' of Braniff's own name for them. Registrations (small, aft) aren't drawn.
